field_rule:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1239) — Under the Flora name Andropogon glomeratus, look for many short flowering branches crowded into a broom-shaped cluster. The Flora gives branch lengths of 1.5–3 cm.

Bushy bluestem is a tufted perennial with erect culms often about 75–150 cm in Kew GrassBase. Numerous crowded short flowering units make a broad, cottony terminal brush, unlike broomsedge's more separated spathe-held units. Texas Uvalde whole-clump and USGS flowering photographs show this gross architecture; a white head alone is not definitive.
trait_provenance: Existing Hays Botany Poaceae species card morphology; preliminary multi-access character states; needs field QA

field_rule:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1243) — Compare the main cane and its full flowering head. The Flora describes usually unbranched canes 2–6 m tall and panicles 30–60 cm long.

The locally archived Forest & Kim Starr Maui stand (panel 0) and Duarte Frade roadside stand (panel 1) show actual tall cane-like culms and long broad clasping leaves. Harry Rose's true attached flowering panicle (panel 4) shows the complete many-branched head. Recognize the large rhizomatous reed, but do not claim any ONE photo proves root-to-head linkage or Texas provenance. A permitted disturbed Texas specimen with roots/canes/head in on

field_rule:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1244) — Count florets within one intact spikelet. The Flora key gives usually three or four.

Begin with the TWO archived Texas in-situ Avena fatua photos (panels 4–5): trace each open, often nodding, branched panicle to the pendent spikelets. Panel 0 adds an older source-identified flowering view. None exposes connected roots or proves the mature floret callus. A 7–40 cm panicle and 2–3-flowered large spikelets are published traits, not independently measured from these photographs. Contrast the unbranched spikes of Hordeum and Secale.

field_rule:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1246) — Trace the axis of the silvery head. In the Flora key it usually extends farther than the individual branches.

Start with Matt Lavin's genuine silvery panicle (panel 0), then see Austin flowering habitat (panel 7). Trace the MANY SHORT crowded hairy flowering branches along a central axis, not just their white hairs. Compare introduced KR (panel 4): several longer finger-like terminal racemes. A detached fuzzy head alone is insufficient.

field_rule: TALL GRAMA B. pectinata is usually robust with 3–5 often relatively long straight combs; B. hirsuta has pronounced branch hairs and bare 'stinger' but can overlap in branch count and rachis tip. Blue grama mostly 1–3 curved eyebrows, spikelets tending to extend to branch tip; Texas grama very short woolly/awned groups; red grama thin wiry small appressed racemes. Avoid a species diagnosis from size or branch count alone.

field_rule: B. rigidiseta typically has several (often about 5–9) SHORT bristly/awned units near the top. Blue grama has only about 1–3 long curved combs. Sideoats grama carries many short pendant oats down a much longer axis. Red grama has narrower, more appressed, often purplish branches and awned spikelets; color alone is not sufficient. If an entire culm/branch cannot be resolved, keep Bouteloua sp.
